newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge 'spies' defect to government.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge 'spies' defect to government.

text.p: Five self-proclaimed Khmer Rouge spies claiming to represent nearly 900 fellow agents said on Wednesday they were ceasing their covert operations to join the Cambodian government.

The five, who gave a news conference at co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh's home, put their number at 886 agents with 590 weapons in Phnom Penh and the southeastern provinces of Kampot and Kompong Speu.
But analysts cast doubt on their story, which they said was more likely a show of political one-upmanship in the deteriorating relations between co-Premiers Ranariddh and Hun Sen.

Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed a fragile coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have been competing for the upper hand in relations with the Khmer Rouge, which has been decimated by defections in the past several months.
Analysts cited a similar news conference in November, when another cell of self-proclaimed spies gathered at the home of Hun Sen to announce the defection of thousands of agents.

"You had a defection from the Cambodian People's Party, and now you have a defection from FUNCINPEC," said one military analyst, referring to Hun Sen's former ruling communist CPP and Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party.
"FUNCINPEC is following CPP for political reasons," the analyst said.
The five men told reporters their cell had not been very active.

"We hid among the people and awaited orders. But we did nothing to the government," said Roh Cheithy, who identified himself as a commander of an underground guerrilla division in existence since 1992.
He said he had never heard of the cell which defected in November at the home of Hun Sen.
The Maoist Khmer Rouge guerrillas, responsible for the "killing fields" reign of terror in the 1970s, reneged on a 1991 U.N.-sponsored peace pact and have been fighting the coalition since 1993.
